minutes.headline: Commission voted by roll call to seek an RTP planning grant for engineering at three conservation sites and a picnic-area grant.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission discussed Hickory Hills Lake concerns about discharge from a water district test well, then parking and access options for Table Rock, the Cowdery wildlife platform road and the Reno property. It voted to authorize a planning grant application for engineering on three sites and to authorize a picnic-area grant application for the Small Town Forest, and approved two certificates of compliance. Minutes were not voted on because the draft was not circulated, and an email/OneDrive migration and enforcement matters were discussed.

public_comment.topic: Asked the commission to require a retention pond and controlled discharge for water pumped from the Lunenburg water district well during a 12-month study, to protect Hickory Hills Lake and wetlands.

budget_items.topic: Matching funds for RTP planning grant
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said the commission would commit matching funds from the timber rights fund, with the state putting up several dollars for each one the commission puts up. Engineering cost was not yet known.
A member asked what engineering would cost for the three sites; the chair said no estimate yet and that the engineer would provide a quote to hold for a year and a quarter.
The chair said the prior year's PO was not closed out, so there is enough money in the Mackie's POs for kiosks and other needs.
The chair said the town pays per commercial Outlook license, which carries drive capacity; cost was not seen as a deciding factor.
The chair doubted whether the RTP grant would pay for a shade pavilion and suggested it be a later phase.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission voted by roll call, all five aye, to apply for an RTP planning grant for engineering at Table Rock, the Cowdery platform road and the Reno property.
It voted unanimously to authorize a grant application for a picnic area at the Small Town Forest.
Two certificates of compliance, for 90 Hemlock Drive and 37 Spring Street, each passed on a five-member roll call.
A resident asked for controlled discharge of water pumped from a water district test well near Hickory Hills Lake; staff will contact the district and it goes on a future agenda.
The December 7 minutes were not voted because the draft was not circulated, and no decision was made on moving from Google Drive to OneDrive.

why_it_matters: The grant applications would put town conservation land money, matched by state funds, toward engineering and a picnic area on public land, and the engineering cost was not yet known when the vote was taken.
The Hickory Hills well discharge question touches a lake and wetlands near homes, and the commission has so far only set it for a later agenda.
watch_next: The chair said engineering quotes would come back for a vote in January if the numbers are available.
The 23 Cove Road owner is to be placed on the first January meeting agenda, and the Hickory Hills well discharge is to go on a future agenda.
